accuracy.evidence: Every sum in the lab, text and items was rechecked by hand: buses 8+2=10, 6+4=10, 9+3=12; hops 9 to 12 (3), 7 to 11 (4), 13 to 16 (3); facts 6+4=10 so 10-6=4, 7+5=12 so 12-7=5, 8+6=14 so 14-6=8; balances 4+5=9, 9=4+5, 7+3=10. The CCSS 1.OA.4 and 1.OA.8 wording and the Year 1 'missing number problems such as 7 = □ − 9' quote match the published documents.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented missing-addend errors: adding the two visible numbers (8 + □ = 10 answered 18), returning the known part or the whole, counting the start number as a hop (12 − 9 = 4), and the operational reading of the equals sign so 9 = 4 + □ gets 13 (Knuth et al.; Falkner, Levi and Carpenter). Each appears as a prediction distractor, a match-card distractor (8 + 10 = □) or a challenge slip.

lab_distinct.evidence: Written for this mechanism, the link between a take-away and an add-on question: a bus whose empty seats show the missing addend and prints both number sentences, a take-away to missing-addend matching board with an adding decoy, a hop track that counts hops from the smaller number, a part-whole bar driven by a known fact, and a balance whose box can sit on either side of the equals sign. Passed the 30% shingle gate against every flag lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The sequence moves from a concrete story (seats to fill) to the equivalence of 10 − 8 and 8 + □ = 10, then to the counting-up strategy, then to deriving a subtraction from a known addition fact, and finally to the equals sign as balance. The child acts first and each success line names the idea just shown, e.g. 'One adding fact gives you two take-away facts'.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with the classic wrong answer as a choice: 8 on and 10 seats (18 tempts adding), hops from 9 to 12 (4 tempts counting the start), 12 − 7 after knowing 7 + 5 = 12 (12 and 19 tempt), and 9 = 4 + □ (13 tempts the answer-comes-next reading). The following step makes the child produce the right answer and the reveal line says whether the guess held.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with seven tagged slips: added both numbers, gave the start part, counted the start number as a hop, read = as 'answer next', gave the whole, chose the slow 13-hop count back, and started counting from 1. Each message names the slip and shows the right reasoning with the numbers in the question, e.g. '9 to 10, 11, 12 is 3 hops'.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK grade -1.2 (family kid target 5.0) with short spoken sentences about a bus, hops and boxes; adult text scores 7.7 (target 10.0) and uses the precise terms unknown addend, part-whole, fact family and finding the difference with plain glosses. Canvas lines stay under ten words and every spoken line repeats the numbers.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler scan and the 12% explanation overlap gate (closest neighbours 459 number bonds and 04 subtraction as taking away stay under the limit). Each kid paragraph adds one idea (the same story, the same question, count up, use a fact) and the adult paragraphs cover standards, the part-whole reason, named mistakes and what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Checked screenshots at 360 px (Android, light) and iPhone 13 (dark) for every step before and during Show me: the 12-seat bus fits in two rows, match cards stay in two columns without clipping, the 8-cell hop track keeps numbers readable after the frog was moved above the number, the balance stacks five cubes per row, and the young class gives 56 px buttons.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate ran axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no violations and no console errors. Every drag has a labelled button twin (One more gets on, the take-away and match cards, numbered hop buttons, answer buttons, Put a cube in and Take one out) and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each spoken line.
